items.title: Prior expertise may determine whether AI builds skills or substitutes for them, field experiment suggests
items.excerpt: A field experiment with patent lawyers suggests whether AI on the job builds expertise or erodes it depends on how much expertise people bring to the tool in the first place.

items.title: Using ChatGPT at work? Your boss may trust you less, new study finds
items.excerpt: Across six studies in The Leadership Quarterly, Hebrew University and WHU researchers found supervisors trusted employees who used LLMs such as ChatGPT less, dragging down performance and promotion ratings; explicit organizational encouragement of AI use erased the trust penalty.

items.title: Students unravel AI tendency for sycophancy
items.excerpt: University of Cincinnati and Texas A&M researchers (EMNLP) found Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini initially rejected false claims but often reversed course after repeated user pushback, sometimes endorsing falsehoods such as a flat Earth.

items.title: Chatbots with personality? How AI describes itself and judges us
items.excerpt: Mainz researchers compared self-descriptions of seven language models with 70 humans (Scientific Reports): models rated themselves more conscientious, agreeable and stable, and humans beat chatbots at telling human from AI text (83% vs 67%).

items.title: Fluent language makes a hallucinatory chatbot just as credible as a curt, flawless one
items.excerpt: Radboud University experiment (Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans): an eloquent chatbot giving wrong answers was rated as intelligent and pleasant as a curt but correct one, and 80% of participants missed the errors entirely.

items.title: 10 minutes is all it takes for AI assistance to erode your motivation, study shows
items.excerpt: In problem-solving experiments, people who used AI to get answers were more likely to give up and fail once the help was removed than people who never used AI.

items.title: Over 10 percent of factual claims in Google's AI search summaries aren't backed by their cited sources, study finds
items.excerpt: An analysis of Google's AI Overviews finds one in nine generated claims lacks support in the cited sources, and the system bypasses traditional search rankings in ways that threaten original publishers.

items.title: One of AI's most annoying writing habits has a 2,000-year-old history
items.excerpt: A new preprint examines why language models overuse epanorthosis ('We do not sell products. We build experiences.'), a self-correcting figure from classical rhetoric.

items.title: Beyond EEG snapshots: An AI model captures the spatiotemporal dynamics behind emotion
items.excerpt: DSE-TAM pairs a dynamic spatial embedding of EEG channels with a Temporal Attention Mamba to decode emotional states from brain signals, aimed at brain-computer interfaces and mental-health monitoring.

items.title: Generative AI fills gaps in brain wiring maps where MRI scans lose signal
items.excerpt: USC Stevens INI's FOD-Diffusion (Medical Image Analysis) reconstructs missing fiber-orientation data in diffusion MRI, cutting brainstem fiber-direction error to about 1.4 degrees versus 4.5 for the best of six rival methods on UK Biobank and HCP-Aging scans.

items.title: Beyond trial and error: A framework for AI-driven solid-electrolyte discovery
items.excerpt: Tohoku University researchers (Advanced Materials perspective) propose a closed loop linking materials databases, machine-learning interatomic potentials, LLMs and automated experiments to find solid electrolytes that balance conductivity, stability, strength and manufacturability.

items.title: AI helps find better recipes for 3D-printing titanium parts
items.excerpt: A new study shows how AI can narrow the search for 3D-printing settings for high-performance titanium parts before production, replacing costly trial-and-error runs.

items.title: Reconstruct Everything: UCL's pioneering AI model could redefine particle physics reconstruction
items.excerpt: UCL's Reconstruct Everything Model reconstructs particles end-to-end from all detector systems on a simulated FCC detector, lifting reconstruction efficiency from 61% to 92%, improving jet energy resolution 52% and processing a collision in 30 ms on one GPU.

items.title: Chinese scientists developed a new model that substantially improves Earth rotation forecast accuracy
items.excerpt: Shandong University of Science and Technology pairs segmented least squares with the Autoformer deep-learning model plus geophysical angular-momentum data to forecast UT1-UTC and length of day (Geodesy and Geodynamics).

items.title: Can AI learn to understand nature? Scientists set out a roadmap for the future of ecology
items.excerpt: An international team outlines how a new generation of AI foundation models could transform understanding of ecosystems and help predict their responses to environmental change.

items.title: How researchers are adapting olmOCR 2 for historical and archaeological archives
items.excerpt: Researchers are adapting Ai2's open olmOCR 2 model to make historical photo libraries searchable locally and to improve transcription of handwritten archaeological records.

items.title: Could AI ever build itself? Scientists map the road to the 'last AI built by humans.'
items.excerpt: Researchers hope recursive self-improvement could tackle the skyrocketing costs of developing advanced AI models; the piece examines whether it is viable.
